findings: RESOLVED PRIOR BLOCKER: missing transport stream now raises ValueError('missing transport stream') before streams.splitlines()[0]; IndexError was added to invoke_handoff_worker's except tuple, and blank-first-line residues fall to json.JSONDecodeError (a ValueError subclass). failure_category is pre-set to REMOTE_PROTOCOL_REJECTED before verify_synthetic_protocol and cleared only on success, so validated_status.json is always written with WORKER_FAILED and the correct category. Regression-tested end-to-end through invoke_handoff_worker by substituting {"outputs": []} for the transport run's tool_result.

Verified block-list MCP response support: list-of-text-block tool_result content is joined, any other block shape raises a clear error, and test_protocol_block_list_and_mutation converts the entire fixture to list form and asserts the verifier still passes.

Verified post-readback mutation rejection for pinned cells: update_cell/delete_cell/move_cell targeting a pinned cell ID after the final get_cells readback raises, execution is required to follow readback, and an injected tamper event is tested. Repeat runs, out-of-order runs, and delete/re-add of the transport cell are all caught by the runs-length, sequence-binding, and newCellId provenance checks.

Verified remote integration tests: test_remote_integration_and_blocked_status drives the mocked CLI with the real captured fixture, covering REMOTE_SYNTHETIC_VALIDATED with protocol_verification attached, REMOTE_PROTOCOL_REJECTED on tampered outputs, and WORKER_BLOCKED via the blocker enum (NONE correctly excluded from valid blocked reasons; BLOCKED never becomes success).

Verified timeout/error categories: failure_category distinguishes WORKER_TIMEOUT, WORKER_LAUNCH_FAILED, WORKER_RESPONSE_REJECTED, and REMOTE_PROTOCOL_REJECTED; timeouts still produce a failure receipt because partial-stdout parsing fails closed while preserving the launch category, and a captured result event after timeout cannot become success (returncode None fails the code check).

Scope safety re-confirmed: capture_cell privately captures Python streams and fd-level subprocess output with fixed-only public output (success, failure, and append-rerun tested); private_dir rejects symlinks, in-checkout, and existing paths; pinned cells and P001 approvals are read-only throughout; prepare-p001 remains PREPARED_NOT_EXECUTED behind the four documented gates; no failure path echoes raw model text into published metadata; result validation requires exact dict equality plus claude-fable-5 model identity.

Non-blocking hardening: the post-readback mutation guard covers only pinned cell IDs, not the supplementary transport cell. A worker could add_code_cell with the correct transport source (satisfying provenance via newCellId), then update_cell that cell to print the expected JSON known from the packet before running it. Delete/re-add is caught; update_cell is not. Extend the guard to runs[3]'s cellId after its add. Synthetic-only; pinned runs still require genuine MCP tool_results, so only the 'actual retrieved bytes' evidence is weakened.

Minor evidence-quality: a validly reported BLOCKED outcome records failure_category WORKER_RESPONSE_REJECTED, mislabeling a well-formed blocked report; status and blocker fields are correct so no false success results.

Minor test/robustness gaps: WORKER_TIMEOUT and WORKER_LAUNCH_FAILED categories lack direct test coverage (the mock CLI always returns 0), and a task_packet/verify_handoff failure before worker launch (e.g., returned_stream[0] on the pinned receipt) crashes with a traceback and no receipt — acceptable fail-loud behavior on pinned committed data, but pre-launch failures leave the freshly created private directory behind, forcing a new --private-dir on retry.
